322800.title: The partial coloring extension conjecture
322800.statement:
Let $G$ be a countable group, let $A \subseteq G$, let $k > 1$ be an integer, and let $y: A \rightarrow k$. A partial coloring is a function defined on $A$, and $\overline{[y]}$ denotes the closure of its orbit in the corresponding coloring space.

**Partial coloring extension conjecture.** Then $y$ can be extended to a $k$-coloring if and only if $\overline{[y]} \cap k^G$ consists of aperiodic points.

This conjecture seeks a complete criterion for extending arbitrary partial colorings to $k$-colorings. The text notes that the criterion has been proved for slender and cofinite domains, but not in full generality.
322800.finding: k-coloring is a source-defined dynamical term, not merely any function G→k (arbitrary functions extend trivially). Need orbit closure topology and robust aperiodicity at every orbit limit. Olshanskii reference is unrelated, not a refutation. Primary body unread.

323001.title: The cycle-length conjecture for necklace dynamics
323001.statement:
For integers $k$ and $n$, let $\operatorname{Neck}(k,n)$ be the directed graph whose vertices are $(k,n)$-necklaces and whose transition map is $T$. A cycle in this graph is a periodic orbit of $T$. **Necklace cycle-length conjecture.** Every cycle in $\operatorname{Neck}(k,n)$ has length dividing $n-3k$. Equivalently, for every $(k,n)$-necklace $N$,

$$
T^{n-3k}N=N.
$$

The map $T$ is already known to be a bijection on the necklace graph, and the boundary cases described immediately before the conjecture are consistent with the claim. The divisibility assertion for general $(k,n)$ remains open in the source.

324898.title: SASE equivalence conjecture for decreasing-increasing patterns
324898.statement:
Let $M(p)$ denote the permutation matrix of a pattern $p$, and set

$$
F_k=M((k-1)(k-2)\cdots1k),\qquad J_k=M(k(k-1)\cdots1).
$$

Here $F_k\underset{1-\text{SASE}}{\sim}J_k$ denotes equivalence under $1$-SASE. **SASE equivalence conjecture.** For all $k>2$, we have $F_k\underset{1-\text{SASE}}{\sim}J_k$. This would fully extend the cited theorem to alternating and reverse alternating permutations; it generalizes earlier results, and empirical data suggests that it generates most equivalences for alternating permutations.
324898.finding: Need exact 1-SASE definition, ascent/descent constraints and a shape-preserving bijection for all k>2. Ordinary permutation Wilf equivalence alone is insufficient. Primary definition/proof and companions unread.

325051.title: Bar 1-visibility conjecture for 1-planar graphs
325051.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. It is **1-planar** if it has a drawing in the plane in which each edge is crossed by at most one other edge. It is **bar 1-visible** if it has a bar 1-visibility drawing: vertices are represented by pairwise disjoint horizontal bars, and each edge is represented by a vertical segment joining the bars of its endpoints and crossing at most one bar belonging to another vertex.

**Bar 1-visibility conjecture.** Every 1-planar graph is a bar 1-visible graph.

The conjecture arises because the authors constructed bar 1-visibility drawings for every 1-planar graph they considered, but did not have a formal proof. The paper gives linear-time constructions for several classes of 1-planar graphs, while the general implication remains open.
325051.finding: A plane visibility construction must handle each crossing, bars and crossing capacity simultaneously, including general not just special 1-planar embeddings. No full construction or obstruction. Original/final/corrections bodies unread; no known-result exclusion asserted.

325163.title: The connected domination bound for connected $(P_9,C_9,H)$-free graphs
325163.statement:
Let $P_9$ denote the path on $9$ vertices, let $C_9$ denote the cycle on $9$ vertices, and let $H$ be the graph shown in Figure H. A graph is $(P_9,C_9,H)$-free if it contains none of these graphs as an induced subgraph. For a graph $G$, let $\gamma(G)$ be its domination number and $\gamma_c(G)$ its connected domination number. **Connected domination conjecture.** For every connected $(P_9,C_9,H)$-free graph $G$, 
$$
\gamma_c(G) \le 2\gamma(G).
$$
 This extends the established bound for connected $(P_8,C_8)$-free graphs; the conjecture concerns whether the same factor-two bound remains valid in the larger class obtained by forbidding $P_9$, $C_9$, and the graph $H$.
325163.finding: Figure H is not encoded in the literal text; no adjacency reconstruction or visual read was done. Need that graph before a fidelity-valid witness or induction. P8/C8 bound does not imply larger forbidden class.

325192.title: The quadratic linkedness conjecture for edge-disjoint Hamilton cycles
325192.statement:
A **tournament** is an orientation of a complete graph, a **Hamilton cycle** is a consistently oriented cycle containing all vertices, and a tournament is **$k$-linked** if it contains vertex-disjoint directed paths joining every prescribed set of $k$ initial vertices to every prescribed set of $k$ terminal vertices in the prescribed pairing.

**Quadratic linkedness conjecture.** There exists $C'>0$ such that, for every $k\in\mathbb{N}$, every $C'k^2$-linked tournament contains $k$ edge-disjoint Hamilton cycles.

The paper proves the corresponding bound with an additional logarithmic factor, so removal of that factor remains open in the supplied text.
325192.finding: No historical tournament lane was opened. Literal record read only. A C k² log k theorem does not furnish an absolute C prime with C prime k² for all k. Universal routing/absorption proof unpaid; public solved label not accepted as proof.

325397.title: The completion invariance conjecture for the $c_2$-invariant
325397.statement:
Let $G_1$ and $G_2$ be primitive-divergent graphs with isomorphic completions, and let $c_2(G_i)_q\in\mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z}$ denote their $c_2$-invariants at a prime power $q$. **Completion invariance conjecture.** Their $c_2$-invariants are equal modulo $q$:

$$
c_2(G_1)_q\equiv c_2(G_2)_q\pmod q
$$

for every prime power $q$. The conjecture is motivated by the fact that graphs with isomorphic completions are proved to have the same period; the source gives no general resolution of the corresponding $c_2$ statement.
325397.finding: All prime powers q and every pair of primitive-divergent completions required. Equal periods do not imply equal point counts modulo q; reference refutation text may concern another conjecture. No actual coefficient/graph witness or all-q bridge.

325430.statement: Let ${\mathfrak{S}}$ be a step set symmetric about an axis $L$, where $L$ passes through the first quadrant, potentially along a boundary. This conjecture concerns the use of symmetry to obtain sharp upper bounds for quarter-plane models of arbitrary step size; experimental evidence motivates it, but the general assertion remains open.

325433.title: The motion conjecture for graphs
325433.statement:
Let $G$ be an infinite graph of arbitrary cardinality. Write $\operatorname{m}(G)$ for its motion, $\operatorname{Aut}(G)$ for its automorphism group, and $\operatorname{D}(G)$ for its distinguishing number.

**Motion conjecture for graphs.** The inequality

$$
2^{\operatorname{m}(G)}\geq |\operatorname{Aut}(G)|
$$

implies

$$
\operatorname{D}(G)=2.
$$

This is the infinite-cardinality form of the Motion Conjecture for Graphs and would extend the Motion Lemma beyond finite automorphism groups. The source presents it as a conjecture and gives no resolution in the stated generality.
325433.finding: DERIVATIONS: C5 plus rigid ray gives m4, Aut10, D3, but finite-motion omission does not solve intended infinite-motion conjecture.

325644.title: Rota's matroid decomposition conjecture
325644.statement: Let ${\mathcal M}$ be a matroid, and let $F_1,\ldots,F_k$ be independent sets in ${\mathcal M}$ with $|F_i|=k$ for every $i$. An ${\mathcal M}$-SR is a system of representatives whose range is independent in ${\mathcal M}$. **Rota's conjecture.** The multiset union $\bigcup_{i=1}^k F_i$ can be decomposed into $k$ ${\mathcal M}$-SRs. This is the decomposition version of the basic matroid representative observation; the source presents it as a famous conjecture and gives no resolution.
325644.finding: Rota full decomposition requires k independent transversals partitioning every occurrence, not just one matroid representative system. Greedy deletion changes rank constraints; no induction preserving residual hypotheses. References confuse Latin-square parity with this claim; not a refutation.

325836.title: Lin's conjecture on ternary ideal two-level autocorrelation sequences
325836.statement:
Let $n=2m+1$, and let $\alpha$ be a primitive element in $\mathbb{F}_{3^n}$. Let $Tr$ denote the trace map from $\mathbb{F}_{3^n}$ to $\mathbb{F}_3$, and define the ternary sequence $S=\{s_i\}$ by

$$
s_i=Tr(\alpha^i+\alpha^{(2\cdot 3^m+1)i}),\qquad i=0,1,2,\ldots.
$$

**Lin's conjecture.** The sequence $S$ has ideal two-level autocorrelation; that is, if its period is $N$, then

$$
C_S(\tau)=\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}\omega_3^{s_{i+\tau}-s_i}=-1
$$

for every $0<\tau<N$.

The paper claims to prove this conjecture using the second-order multiplexing decimation-Hadamard transform, Stickelberger's theorem, the Teichmüller character, and elementary enumeration of ternary numbers. Thus the conjecture is presented as solved in the source paper.
325836.finding: Actual source Conjecture1 and Theorem5 say the same Lin sequence has ideal autocorrelation. Proof opening and dependency route read, not all ternary-weight proof; no independent formal audit or new result. Formula exact including 2*3^m+1.

325944.title: The one-third approval-ratio conjecture for double-interval societies
325944.statement:
A **double-interval society** is a society in which each voter's approval set is the union of two intervals, and a society is **pairwise-intersecting** when every two voters' approval sets intersect. For such a society $S$, let $a(S)$ denote its approval ratio and let $n$ denote the number of voters.

**One-third approval-ratio conjecture.** For all pairwise-intersecting double-interval societies $S$, the approval ratio

$$
\frac{a(S)}{n} \geq \frac13.
$$

This conjecture is the authors' initial conjecture, for which they report additional supporting evidence. Its resolution is not established in the supplied text.

326137.title: Krause–Zahlten's cross number conjecture for finite abelian groups
326137.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group. Write

$$
G=\bigoplus_{i=1}^{r}C_{p_i^{\alpha_i}}
$$

with each summand of prime-power order, and define

$$
\mathsf{k}^{*}(G)=\sum_{i=1}^{r}\left(1-\frac{1}{p_i^{\alpha_i}}\right).
$$

Let $\mathsf{K}^{*}(G)=\mathsf{k}^{*}(G)+1/\operatorname{exp}(G)$, where $\operatorname{exp}(G)$ is the exponent of $G$. **Krause–Zahlten's conjecture.** The equality $\mathsf{K}(G)=\mathsf{K}^{*}(G)$ holds for all finite abelian groups $G$, and therefore $\mathsf{k}(G)=\mathsf{k}^{*}(G)$ for all $G$ as well. The conjecture gives the expected values of the cross-number invariants for arbitrary finite abelian groups; the cited context reports structural progress but no resolution.
326137.finding: Need all finite abelian groups, including mixed primes, and all minimal zero-sum sequences. Prime-power structural bounds do not yield global cross-number bound. No weighting/merging argument controlling cross-prime orders; actual source body unread.

326679.title: Cyclic Hamiltonian-path decomposition conjecture for Cayley multigraphs
326679.statement:
Let $\mathbb{Z}_v$ be the cyclic group of order $v$, let $L$ be a list of edge-lengths, and let $Cay[\mathbb{Z}_v:\Lambda]$ denote the corresponding Cayley multigraph. **Cyclic decomposition conjecture.** A Cayley multigraph $Cay[\mathbb{Z}_v:\Lambda]$ admits a cyclic decomposition into Hamiltonian paths if and only if

$$
\Lambda=L\cup -L
$$

with $L$ satisfying the divisor condition that, for every divisor $d$ of $v$, the number of multiples of $d$ appearing in $L$ is at most $v-d$. This is presented as a reformulation of the Horak–Rosa Hamiltonian-path conjecture and is therefore open in the same generality.
326679.finding: Necessary divisor count does not construct one Hamilton path with the exact multiset of lengths; developing all translates would only work after that path exists. List cardinality v-1 and source multiplicity/signed conventions require primary-body fidelity. No sufficiency proof.

326698.title: Strong-geometry conjecture for geometric preferential attachment
326698.statement:
For $\gamma>1$, define

$$
F_\gamma(r)=\exp\{(\log(1/r))^\gamma\},
$$

where $\log x=\max\{0,\log x\}$. Let $G_n$ be the geometric preferential attachment graph under the paper's standing assumptions, let $v_n$ be the vertex selected by the new vertex, and let $\eta_1(n)$ be its on-line nearest neighbour. **Strong-geometry conjecture.** The conclusion of Theorem 1(ii), including convergence to the on-line nearest-neighbour degree sequence, is valid for every $\gamma>1$. The theorem establishes this conclusion for $\gamma>3/2$; extending it to the full range $\gamma>1$ remains open, as does the stronger almost-sure convergence discussed in the surrounding remark.

326843.title: The universal quandle-coloring separation conjecture
326843.statement:
Let $\mathcal S=(Q_1,Q_2,\ldots)$ be a sequence of finite quandles, and define the coloring invariant

$$
C(K)=\bigl(\operatorname{Col}_{Q_1}(K),\operatorname{Col}_{Q_2}(K),\ldots\bigr).
$$

**Universal quandle-coloring separation conjecture.** There exists such a sequence satisfying, for all knots $K,K' $,

$$
C(K')=C(K)\quad\text{if and only if}\quad K'=K\text{ or }K'=mr(K).
$$

This is a stronger global form of the finite-knot separation problem and is presented as an open conjecture; the paper gives finite computational evidence but does not establish the assertion for all knots.
326843.finding: Finite-knot coloring tests do not separate all knots modulo mirror-reverse. Requires finite quandle quotients and distinguishing homomorphism counts, with equivalence in both directions; residual finiteness alone not enough. No all-knot construction.

326883.title: Fixed-graph recurrence conjecture for simple random walk on growing subgraphs
326883.statement: Let $\bmathbb{G}_\infty$ be a fixed graph of uniformly bounded degrees on which simple random walk is recurrent, and let $\bmathbb{G}_t$ be non-decreasing subgraphs with $\bmathbb{G}_t\uparrow\bmathbb{G}_\infty$. **Fixed-graph recurrence conjecture.** Simple random walk on $\bmathbb{G}_t$ is recurrent for any choice of such non-decreasing $\bmathbb{G}_t$. This is presented as a consequence of the monotonicity conjecture and would imply recurrence for simple random walk on every non-decreasing subgraph evolution in $\bmathbb{Z}^2$. The claim remains open in the source.
326883.finding: Static recurrence or Rayleigh monotonicity does not control a time-dependent transition kernel or adversarial growth. Need evolution-specific return/supermartingale bounds or explicit uniformly bounded-degree recurrent-limit witness; no such full route. No denied randomwalk source retried.

354641.title: Jaeger et al.'s group-connectivity analogue of the 3-flow conjecture
354641.statement:
For an abelian group $\Gamma$, a graph $G$ is **$\Gamma$-connected** if $(G,\beta)$ has a nowhere-zero flow for every $\Gamma$-boundary $\beta$. **Jaeger et al.'s group-connectivity conjecture.** Every $5$-edge-connected graph is $\mathbb{Z}_3$-connected.
